#Accessibility

Wren is read by screen readers (NVDA, Narrator, JAWS) and other assistive technologies through UI Automation. The toolkit makes the accessibility tree of the interface from its boxes and hands it to AccessKit (ext/gui_toolkit/docs/accessibility.md); Wren says what only a browser knows.

#Build

The assembly crate native/wren_native builds the toolkit's adapter (ext/gui_toolkit/native/a11y, AccessKit 0.25 and its Windows adapter) into wren_native.lib (feature a11y: a program links one Rust static library; see docs/architecture.md, "The Rust library"), and build.bat builds with -define:A11Y_ACCESSKIT=true -define:A11Y_NATIVE_LINK=false. The crates are listed in native/rust-crates.txt (about:licenses).

Nothing is built until an assistive technology asks for a window's tree; from then on each frame sends the nodes that changed. wren ctl stats --json says what was sent: a11yUpdates, a11yRefused, a11yLastNodes, a11yNodes.

#The interface

PartRoleWhat it says
Tab strip, tab sidebarTabList ("Tabs", horizontal / vertical)
A tabTabthe page's title (else its address, else "New tab"), selected, "3 of 12", busy while loading; its close button inside
Back, Forward, Reload, New tab, Menu, the blocker's shield, Page informationButtonnamed by their tooltip, its shortcut (Alt+Left, F5, Ctrl+T...), the tooltip as description; disabled when they cannot act; Menu: expanded, has a menu
Address barEdit ("Address and search bar", Ctrl+L)its text, caret and selection (text runs), the placeholder; while suggestions show: expanded, controls the list, the chosen suggestion read as the focus
SuggestionsListBox of ListBoxOptionstitle, address, what Enter does
Menus (main menu, context menus)Menu, MenuItemthe commands' titles and shortcuts, checked items, submenus
Caption buttonsButtonMinimize, Maximize / Restore, Close (i18n.tr)
Status barStatusits items as text, their tooltips as descriptions
ToastsAlert / Statusannounced when they appear
Sidebar's resize handleSplitterthe width
DevToolsTab per panel, Buttonsthe panels' titles; buttons named by their tooltips, toggles say on / off

The names go through i18n.tr (the tooltips of the chrome were already its texts). The helpers are in src/browser/a11y_chrome.odin: chrome_tip_a11y (a button named by its tooltip: "Back (Alt+Left); right click: history" is "Back", shortcut "Alt+Left"), tab_a11y, tab_list_a11y.

#Pages

The current page is a tree of its own (src/a11y, package a11y), grafted under the page area (A11y_Info.graft, tree id from the tab's id: page_tree_id) and sent after the chrome's tree (src/browser/a11y_page.odin).

  • Roles (roles.odin): the implicit roles of HTML-AAM (links with href, buttons, every input type, select as combo box or list box, textarea, headings, landmarks with their scoping rules for header / footer, section and form only when named, lists, description lists, tables with row and column headers, img (alt="" is decoration), figure, details / summary, dialog, fieldset / legend, label, progress, meter, output...) and the ARIA role attribute (first known token; none / presentation ignored on focusable elements and those with global ARIA).
  • Names and descriptions (name.odin, Accessible Name and Description Computation 1.2): aria-labelledby (hidden referenced text counts), aria-label, the host language (labels for and around, alt, caption, legend, figcaption, the value of input buttons, "Submit" / "Reset", title of frames, option labels), the content for the roles named by it (embedded controls give their value, block elements are separated), title, then placeholder; descriptions from aria-describedby, aria-description or title.
  • States and properties: disabled (also through a disabled fieldset), checked / mixed / pressed, selected, expanded (aria-expanded, a details' summary), required, read only, multiselectable, busy, modal, level, "3 of 7" (aria-posinset/setsize or the place among siblings), values (range, number, progress, meter, aria-value*), text field values (a password is not read), placeholder, link URL, aria-current, aria-invalid, aria-haspopup, aria-orientation, aria-controls / details / flowto / owns, aria-activedescendant, aria-errormessage, aria-keyshortcuts, aria-roledescription, lang; tables: row and column counts, row and column indexes, spans.
  • Left out: display: none, aria-hidden="true", hidden, inert; visibility: hidden elements are not nodes (their visible children are).
  • Live regions: aria-live, roles alert (assertive), status and log (polite): their text is their name, so AccessKit raises a live region event when it changes.
  • Focus: the page's focused element (the forms' focus) while the page has the keyboard (ui.a11y_focus_on the page area).
  • Text fields: their text as a text run (reading by character and word: Word_Starts), their caret and selection (Text_Selection, from the forms' selection, in characters of the run); a selection made by the reader (Set_Text_Selection) moves the field's (forms.set_selection).
  • Frames: the document of an iframe is a tree of its own (tree id from its stand-in tab), grafted under the frame element's node (View.frame_tree) and sent after its parent's, only when the parent's tree has that graft node; its transform places it in the frame's content box. Requests for its nodes act in the frame's document; the focus follows the frame that has the keyboard (the graft node, then the frame's own focus). Frames of frames too. accessibility.page.frames turns them off.
  • Shadow trees: the composed tree (a host's shadow root, a slot's assigned nodes).
  • Bounds: from the layout (layout.box_of_view, document coordinates; the document node's transform is the page area's place and the scroll: scrolling changes one node). A text node has the union of the display items that show it (its lines, layout.item_rect).
  • Actions of screen readers: click (a synthetic click, as HTMLElement.click(): page.click_element), focus (forms.focus), set value (forms.set_value, as typed: input events), increment / decrement (forms.step, as the arrow keys), scroll into view, scroll up / down.
  • Updates, node by node (incremental.odin, a11y.live_update): after a document's first whole tree, an update holds only the nodes a change reaches, written whole and handed to platform.a11y_diff_patch. What changed comes from what the engine records already: the mutation journal (dom.journal_since), the style journal's Box-level changes (style.journal_since: display, visibility), a hash of each form control's value, checkedness, selectedness and selection, Document.listener_changes (what a click acts on), the geometry (the layout's passes, the viewport; on a scroll alone, only the boxes fixed to the viewport), the title, the address and the focus. A change is handled at the nearest node above it, walked again with the unchanged nodes below it taken as they are; what may depend on it is written again one by one: the ancestors (names from content, live regions), list items (their place in the set), the rows and cells of a table, the nodes pointing at an id (aria-labelledby, -describedby, -controls, -activedescendant...), the controls of a <label for>. What the journals cannot say (a journal that forgot, more than accessibility.page.max_nodes, a box gone, visibility or display animated) makes a whole tree (then diffed). Nothing is built or sent while nothing changes. accessibility.page.verify compares every update with a whole tree (a11y.live_verify; wren ctl stats: a11yPageVerifyFailed, a11yPageVerifyDiff); accessibility.page.incremental off makes every update a whole tree.
  • Windows: each window keeps its page's trees (Window_Own.a11y): two windows show two pages.
  • Preferences: accessibility.page.enabled, .incremental, .verify, .max_nodes (50 000), .frames.

Not done yet (next steps):

  • Static text read character by character, and the page's own text selection: text nodes are Label nodes with a value, without text runs (AccessKit reads character by character only inside text runs); a document-level text selection (the page's Selection mapped to runs) needs runs for static text and, in the toolkit's adapter, selections whose positions are runs deeper than the node's children (gt_a11y only accepts runs that are its direct children, AccessKit panics on a position that is not a run).
  • Character positions and widths of the runs of text fields (Character_Positions): ranges have the field's bounds.
  • A text in a box fixed to the viewport keeps its bounds at scroll 0 (its lines are measured at scroll 0).

#Testing

  • src/a11y unit tests (in test_all): the tree of examples/a11y/page.html (a form, a list, a table, a dialog, live regions, ARIA tabs, hidden parts) against the expected roles, names and states, and the name computation's precedence.
  • src/tools/e2e/a11y.odin (in test_all, no window at all): what a window tells a screen reader, read as it is handed to the adapter (control_a11y_tree) and acted on as a reader's requests are (control_a11y_act): the chrome's roles, names and states, New tab, the address bar's value, selecting a tab, expanding and collapsing the menu; examples/a11y/page.html: its document, controls, states, what is left out, and setting a field, toggling a check box and focusing a field act on the page; examples/a11y/dynamic.html: nodes the page inserts, renames, adds and removes; a text's bounds are its line's; a frame's button acts in the frame; a selection made by the reader; a second window has its own page.
  • src/tools/e2e/a11y_uia.odin (in test_all): a Wren with a real window, never shown, read and driven through the system's UI Automation, as a screen reader does (toolkit:tools/uia): the chrome's elements and the patterns that act; examples/a11y/dynamic.html with accessibility.page.verify on: changes go as patches equal to whole trees, nothing is built or sent at rest, no update refused; a frame's button is invoked in the frame; a field's text and selection through the text pattern; a second window reads its own page.
  • src/a11y incremental tests: every patch applied as an adapter would (refusing a node no parent reaches, a missing child, a node twice) and compared with a whole tree, for scripted changes (text, attributes, list items, a wrapper at the top, aria-hidden, roles, aria-labelledby targets, <label for>, a table row, title, focus, a listener) and 60 pseudo-random ones.
  • By hand: odin build ext\gui_toolkit\tools\uia_probe -out:build\uia_probe.exe, then build\uia_probe.exe dump --pid <pid of wren.exe> prints every element as a screen reader sees it.
  • With a person: NVDA and Narrator (what they say, browse and focus modes): see the session note of 2026-10-26.
